submissions.findingTextShort: A migraine-prophylaxis systematic review found moderate evidence from two proprietary Petadolex trials, with long-term safety still needing confirmation.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review of butterbur for migraine prophylaxis included two trials representing 293 patients, both using the proprietary Petadolex preparation. The review found moderate evidence for the higher-dose extract while noting the need for longer-term safety confirmation. This evidence is product-specific and must not be generalized to raw butterbur, unverified extracts or products containing pyrrolizidine alkaloids.
submissions.populationContext: Migraine-prophylaxis patients represented in two clinical trials / 293 participants.
submissions.usageContext: Proprietary Petadolex butterbur extract; preparation identity and PA status are material.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Small number of trials and long-term safety uncertainty limit broad conclusions.

submissions.findingTextShort: A three-arm migraine RCT found 75 mg twice daily proprietary butterbur extract superior to placebo, while 50 mg twice daily was not clearly superior.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized three-arm migraine-prophylaxis trial in 245 patients found a favorable result for 75 mg twice daily of the proprietary butterbur root extract, while the 50 mg twice-daily arm did not clearly outperform placebo. The dose-dependent contrast is important and must remain attached to the studied verified extract rather than becoming a generic butterbur dose recommendation.
submissions.populationContext: Two hundred forty-five migraine patients in a randomized three-arm trial.
submissions.usageContext: Proprietary butterbur root extract at 50 mg or 75 mg twice daily; verified preparation context required.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: One dose arm was not clearly positive; do not flatten the trial into a generic yes/no efficacy statement.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 real-world Petamig study reported favorable within-person migraine outcomes in 120 patients but lacked a control group.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2026 uncontrolled real-world study of the proprietary Petamig preparation in 120 migraine patients reported favorable within-person outcomes. Because there was no control group, the study cannot establish comparative efficacy or upgrade certainty above the randomized evidence. Product identity and verified PA-free status remain essential.
submissions.populationContext: One hundred twenty migraine patients in an uncontrolled real-world study.
submissions.usageContext: Proprietary Petamig butterbur product; uncontrolled observational treatment context.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: No control group; regression to the mean, placebo effects and concomitant care cannot be excluded.

submissions.findingTextShort: Hepatobiliary safety/toxicogenomics work reinforces that butterbur extract identity and pyrrolizidine-alkaloid control are safety-critical.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Hepatobiliary safety/toxicogenomics evidence on butterbur extracts reinforces that extraction process, product identity and pyrrolizidine-alkaloid content are safety-critical variables. The evidence does not make every marketed 'PA-free' label equivalent or prove long-term clinical safety, but it supports retaining a hard firewall between specifically verified PA-free preparations and raw/unverified butterbur products.
submissions.safetyContext: Pyrrolizidine-alkaloid and hepatobiliary safety identity; preparation verification is required before any consumer-facing reassurance.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Preclinical/toxicogenomic safety evidence cannot quantify long-term human incidence; product verification remains necessary.
